summary: Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Harvard. He held a post at UC Berkeley (circa 1947–1984) and served as president of the American Oriental Society (1975–1976).

Edward H. Spieker worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying at Baltimore City College and earning his A.B. and Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins University, he served there as Associate Professor of Greek and Latin from 1880 to 1918.

An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Edward Hamilton Johnston studied at Eton, New College, and the University of Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1909–1921) and became Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit in 1937.

Edward Henry Palmer worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Sayyid Abdallah and at St John's College, Cambridge, later serving as Cambridge's Lord Almoner’s Professor of Arabic from 1871 to 1881.
Edward Hincks was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He was educated at Midleton College and Trinity College Dublin, where he earned his B.A. between 1807 and 1812.

Edward James Rapson specialized in Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge, he worked at the British Museum (1887–1906), UCL (1903–1906), and as Cambridge's Professor of Sanskrit (1906–1936).

Edward John Thompson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Richmond College and Kingswood School, taught at Bankura Christian College from 1910, lectured in Bengali at Oxford from 1923, and was a Research Fellow at Oriel College (1936–1940).

Edward Joseph Thomas was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St Andrews under John Burnet and at Emmanuel College, Cambridge. He served as Head and Librarian of the Cambridge University Library's Oriental Department.

Edward Kamens is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University (circa 1974–1982) and later served on its faculty from 1986 to 2022, becoming Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures.

Edward Klich was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Jan Michał Rozwadowski at Jagiellonian University between circa 1898 and 1902. In 1929, he became a professor at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań.
Edward Lavallin Puxley was active in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Brasenose College, Oxford, in 1852 and served as a missionary for the Church Mission Society from 1859 to 1866.

Edward Lucas Hogarth was an Indologist who studied at Brasenose College, Oxford. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Oxford and served as Head Master at the Government Provincial School in Calicut from circa 1868 to 1876.
Edward Payson Newton worked in linguistics and Indology. He pursued his education at Princeton University from circa 1866 to 1870 and at Pittsburgh Theological Seminary from circa 1870 to 1873.
Edward Peter Rice worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Cheshunt College and the University of London, and served with the London Missionary Society from 1873 to 1915.

Edward Rehatsek studied civil engineering at Eötvös Loránd University. Active in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he was a professor at the University of Breslau and Wilson College, Mumbai, and an examiner at the University of Mumbai (1869–1881).

Edward Ross specializes in Buddhist studies, computational studies, and religious studies. He studied at McGill University, the University of Hong Kong, and the University of Reading, where he served as an Associate Lecturer from 2020 to 2025.
Edward Russell Ayrton was an archaeologist and Indologist. He was educated at St Paul's School, studied under Flinders Petrie, and held a post at Abydos from circa 1902 to 1904.

Philosopher Edward S. Casey studied at Yale, the Sorbonne, and Northwestern, and under Paul Ricœur. He taught at Yale, UCSB, and Stony Brook University, where he was Dean of the Faculty of Philosophy circa 1978.

Linguist Edward Sapir studied at Columbia University under Franz Boas. He served at the Geological Survey of Canada (1910–1925), the University of Chicago (circa 1925–1931), and became Sterling Professor of Anthropology and Linguistics at Yale in 1931.

Edward Thomas was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College from circa 1830 to 1832 and served as a writer in the Bengal Civil Service from 1832 to 1857.
